main_topics.reason: The user came to understand the options and repeatedly asked what might guide the choice of a biologic.
The user called long-term risk the question that scared them most and discussed the risk-benefit of treatment at length.
The user raised recurrent sinus infections and prior shingles and asked whether these would steer treatment selection.
The user described persistent hand and wrist synovitis and prolonged morning stiffness as evidence of active disease.
The user reported CRP levels around 18–20 for months as part of the picture of ongoing disease activity.
The user compared home injections with infusions because frequent work travel affects which option seems practical.
The user asked how long it takes to know whether a biologic is working and did not want to endure months without a checkpoint.
The user briefly mentioned being needle-shy while considering self-injection.
The user asked whether possible hormone therapy could interact with RA treatment in one exchange.

output.summary: The user wanted to understand biologic options before a rheumatology appointment, describing persistent synovitis and stiffness despite methotrexate and sulfasalazine. The assistant discussed treatment classes, infection and shingles considerations, travel logistics, long-term risks, response timelines, and questions to take to the clinician. The user said they felt prepared for a back-and-forth with the rheumatologist and that the conversation lowered their anxiety.
